issues.legal_issue: An accused should not be discharged at the preliminary stage when the allegations, if true, disclose the charged offences and the preliminary record makes out a prima facie case, merely because the dispute also involves civil title.
material_facts: The complaint alleged that the accused trespassed on an orchard, destroyed it, and removed trees, and charged them with offences including mischief, criminal trespass, and theft committed with common intention.
The complainant gave evidence and produced revenue records and witnesses concerning possession of the land.
The preliminary court found a prima facie case against some accused, and the Magistrate declined to discharge them.
The High Court discharged the accused after relying on the history and outcome of civil litigation concerning the land.
issues.conclusion: The High Court erred in discharging the accused under Section 253(2) of the CrPC. The discharge order was set aside and the trial was directed to proceed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 253(2) of the CrPC, where the allegations, if true, disclose the offences charged and the preliminary material makes out a prima facie case, the accused must stand trial. The possibility of a dispute over civil title does not justify discharge on these facts; the Supreme Court did not decide the title question. The alleged offences were under Sections 427, 447, 379 and 34 of the IPC. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.criminal_complaint_discharge_proceeding: A criminal complaint is before the court and an application seeks discharge of the accused at the preliminary stage.
predicates.allegations_if_true_disclose_charged_off: The complaint alleges conduct which, if true, constitutes the offences charged.
predicates.preliminary_record_supports_allegations: The preliminary evidence and material support the complaint allegations sufficiently to make out a prima facie case.
predicates.accused_must_stand_trial: The accused are not discharged at the preliminary stage and the prosecution proceeds to trial.

issues.definition: When a criminal complaint's allegations would constitute the charged offences and the preliminary record supports them, the accused must stand trial.
